landmarks.name: Kaieteur Falls
landmarks.writeup: One of the world's most powerful waterfalls, located on the Potaro River in the Kaieteur National Park.

landmarks.name: St. George's Cathedral
landmarks.writeup: An Anglican cathedral in Georgetown, known as one of the tallest wooden churches in the world.

landmarks.name: Iwokrama Forest
landmarks.writeup: A protected rainforest reserve known for biodiversity and conservation efforts.

cultural_events.name: Mashramani
cultural_events.writeup: An annual festival celebrating Guyana's Republic Day with music, dance, and colorful parades.

cultural_events.name: Phagwah
cultural_events.writeup: A Hindu spring festival also known as Holi, celebrated with vibrant colors and community gatherings.

food_writeup: Guyanese cuisine is a blend of African, Indian, Amerindian, and European influences, featuring dishes like pepperpot, roti, and cook-up rice.
brief_history: Originally inhabited by indigenous peoples, Guyana was colonized by the Dutch and later the British. It gained independence in 1966 and became a republic in 1970.
current_conflicts: Ongoing territorial dispute with Venezuela over the Essequibo region.
